g10-geography-ug6-t1.overview: Overview of Global Population Change sits inside Human-Natural Environment Interactions. Human-environment interaction is the focus of Unit 6 of Grade 10 Geography in the Ethiopian (FDRE Ministry of Education) curriculum. First, it reviews global population change and why sub-Saharan Africa now grows so fast. Then it explains why people depend on the environment for food, water, shelter, and clothing. Next, it weighs two classic theories, environmental determinism and environmental possibilism. Also it shows how people modify the land, for better and for worse, and how they adapt to change. Finally, it highlights the indigenous knowledge that African communities use to conserve nature. Students will also learn how human-environment interaction applies to real-life situations, such as farming, conservation, and daily survival.
objectives: Describe global population change and Africa’s recent rapid growth.
Explain why humans depend on the environment for survival.
Compare environmental determinism and environmental possibilism.
Analyze how people modify and adapt to the environment.
Identify the types of adaptation to environmental change.

  • Also the twentieth-century population boom across the developing world.
